topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and establishes its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic origins and clonal evolution of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arise and enable susceptible cells to evolve into cancers within permissive environments.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and interpretation of the evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer risk and how evidence for that contribution is interpreted.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive carcinogenesis, developing Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage from environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage that can become mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require a separate promotional process for tumours to develop.

topics.label: Carcinogen susceptibility and recap of causal mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete the account of context-dependent carcinogenesis through developmental susceptibility and then consolidate the mechanisms already introduced.

topics.label: Methods for investigating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenicity can be investigated and why the available evidence and tests have limitations.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This closing consolidates the lecture’s conclusions and frames everyday exposure decisions as risk–benefit judgments.
